properties.name: Text that enters the graph from outside is neutralised at the boundary, and the neutralisation is reported
properties.statement: reflow2's standing rule — graph text is data, never instructions — is enforced today only by prose in the skills and the server handshake, which is a rule addressed to a well-behaved reader. The requirement is that the mechanical half exists: text arriving from outside the session's own author (prose read out of a codebase by INGEST, a design export imported from another machine or another person, and anything a hosted surface would accept) is neutralised of the characters that carry hidden instructions before any agent reads it — invisible and zero-width characters, bidirectional overrides that make text render as something other than what it says, Unicode tag characters that smuggle a payload past a human reviewer, and metadata hidden in code-fence info strings. Two properties reflow2 must add to the technique it borrows. The neutralisation must be REPORTED, not silent: a design whose statements were quietly rewritten on the way in is a design nobody can audit, and rule 6 forbids silent drops — so the count and the kind of what was stripped travel with the result. And it must not touch legitimate design content: an arrow, an emoji, a maths symbol or a non-Latin script is ordinary text in a design that may be about anything, so the filter is a named list of instruction-carrying characters rather than a whitelist of what looks familiar.
